Our Growth Story

We give back to the needy community.

From Three Hungry Children to a Sanctuary of Hope: The Inspiring Rise of Kumi’s Happy Children’s Home

What began in 2023 as a desperate knock on a personal compound door in Kumi by three young, abandoned brothers looking for chores in exchange for a meal has blossomed into a vital lifeline for over 40 vulnerable youth. Happy Children’s Home has transformed from a single household's act of compassion into a thriving sanctuary, rescuing orphans and children of single mothers from the grips of extreme poverty, child labor, and family breakdown to restore their dignity through education, healthcare, and unconditional love.

Read Our Story
What We Do
Education

We ensure zero children drop out due to poverty by providing school essential such as uniforms, exercise books,fees, bags, pens, and pencils to keep them learning safely.

Nutrition

Healthy development requires proper nourishment. We supply regular, nutritious daily meals to support healthy physical growth, learning focus, and mental development.

Clothing

We restore personal dignity and health by providing decent everyday clothing, sweaters, sturdy shoes, and protective sandals for everyday community life.

Shelter

Providing a safe space to lay their heads. We equip children with safe accommodation including clean mattresses, warm blankets, bedsheets, and protective mosquito nets.

Medical Care

We bridge the health gap by offering immediate access to necessary healthcare, medical checkups, emergency treatments, and essential wellness support services.

Vocational Skills

Empowering youth with practical skills for a self-reliant future through hands-on training and community-based vocational programs.

See All Services

From Child Labor to Learning: 14-Year-Old Martha’s Battle for Her Siblings’ Future Sparks Urgent Call for Community Support

When a tragic construction accident left her father paralyzed, 14-year-old Martha and her brother Isaac were forced into manual labor in community gardens just to buy basic school supplies and feed their family. Now, backed by the lifeline of Happy Children’s Home, this resilient young girl and her three siblings are fighting to escape the cycle of extreme hardship, prompting a powerful community appeal for school fees, medical care, and necessities to protect their right to an education and restore their chance to dream.

Our Story

Happy Children's Home is a community-based organization dedicated to giving back to those in need. We empower orphans and vulnerable children to achieve their goals by supporting their education with  scholastic essentials, alongside practical vocational skills training.

It Started With Three Children

I never planned to open an orphanage. It all started at my own house in Kumi.

​

Three young children, Allan, Shadrack, and Elvis, would come to my compound every morning. They were not coming to play. Instead, they were looking for any small chore, such as sweeping, fetching water, or washing, just so I could give them food and some money for school materials. Abandoned by a father struggling with addiction, their mother fled because of the unbearable situation, leaving the children with a sickly grandfather who is also a widower. With no proper care at home, their clothes were torn and their shoes were broken, but they still wanted to go to school.

​

They touched my heart, so I started by helping just those three. I gave them food, books, and the courage to study. Soon after, they brought two friends, Asio and Faith, bringing the number to five. Not long after that, I met Shellah, who was frequently missing school alongside her two younger siblings because their mother had suffered a mental imbalance following a serious accident. As children naturally follow one another, I soon began noticing new faces. I realized there were over 40 children in the village living the same life. Hunger and dropping out of school were a daily reality for these orphans, children of single mothers, and youth affected by illness, HIV, alcohol abuse, or family breakdown.

​

I could not turn them away, nor could I turn my eyes and heart away from them. I gathered them together and talked with them in a parental way to learn more about their backgrounds. Their stories were heartbreaking. I took the initiative to visit some of their homes and invited their guardians and single parents to my house to agree on how we could help these vulnerable children. That is exactly how Happy Children's Home was born in 2023.

Today, what started with three children has extended to 40 children. Our vision is to give them what every child deserves, including education, food, healthcare, and love, so they can become self-reliant and productive citizens.

From Three to Forty

We moved quickly to assist them with food and books, and they soon brought friends, Asio and Faith. Within a short time, we met Shellah and her two younger siblings, whose family fell into crisis after their mother suffered a severe accident. Soon, new faces continued to arrive. We realised that over 40 children in the village were enduring the same harsh realities: going hungry, falling behind due to parental illness, alcohol abuse, or total family breakdown, and dropping out of school entirely. Choosing not to turn our hearts away, we initiated parental community assessments and brought guardians together. Today, Happy Children's Home provides a safe ecosystem offering education, food, healthcare, and absolute love to help vulnerable youth grow into independent, productive citizens.

Martha's Journey

Martha is a 14-year-old girl and one of four children in her family. She has three siblings: Hellen, Benjamin, and Isaac. The children are currently supported by Happy Children’s Home, where they receive care, encouragement, and the opportunity to continue their education and build a better future.

​

Several years ago, their father tragically fell from a roof while doing construction work, sustaining a severe spinal injury that left him unable to walk. This unfortunate accident marked the beginning of serious hardships for the family. Since then, they have struggled to afford basic necessities, including food, clothing, school fees, and essential scholastic materials.

Because of these financial challenges at home, Martha and her brother Isaac have had to work in community gardens to earn money to support their education and help meet some of the family’s daily needs. At such a young age, they carry heavy responsibilities that no child should have to bear.

​

Their younger siblings, Hellen and Benjamin, also face difficulties accessing education because the family cannot consistently afford school fees and academic requirements. Through Happy Children’s Home, the children have found a place of hope where they receive support to continue pursuing their studies.

​

However, the needs of these children remain great. They require urgent assistance with school fees, scholastic materials, food, clothing, medical care, and other basic necessities.

We appeal to compassionate individuals, organizations, and well-wishers to stand with Martha and her siblings. Your support can help keep these children in school, protect them from child labor, provide for their basic needs, and give them the opportunity to grow into independent and responsible adults.

​

When you support a child, you are not only meeting a need today; you are helping to build a brighter tomorrow. Together, we can give Martha, Hellen, Benjamin, and Isaac hope, dignity, education, and a chance to dream again.

Meet the Founders
Lanyero Irene Okot
FOUNDER

Lanyero Irene Okot established this platform out of a profound desire to uplift lives and create lasting positive change within the community. Driven by a vision of inclusivity and shared progress she channels her energy into building spaces where everyone can thrive. Her leadership ensures that the organization always stays grounded in empathy and remains dedicated to serving others transparently.

Opio Joseph Ekodeu
CO-FOUNDER

Opio Joseph Ekodeu co founded this project to turn a shared passion for community empowerment into actionable real world impact. He works closely with local initiatives to ensure our programs are structured effectively and reach the people who need them most. His commitment is fueled by the belief that collective unity and supportive infrastructure can unlock the full potential of our society.

Our Legal Status

Officially Registered & Verified Happy Children’s Home is a fully registered Community-Based Organisation (CBO) operating in Kumi District, Uganda. We are committed to complete transparency, accountability, and the legal safeguarding of the vulnerable children and families we serve.

Whether it is providing a school bag, a pair of uniform shoes, a warm blanket, or a financial sponsorship contribution, every single gift creates immediate, lasting change. Partner with Happy Children's Home today to replace despair with hope.
